original_value: Automated oscillometric blood pressure monitors are commonly used to measure blood pressure for many patients at home, office, and medical centers, and they have been actively studied recently. These devices usually provide a single blood pressure point and they are not able to indicate the uncertainty of the measured quantity. We propose a new technique using an ensemble-based recursive methodology to measure uncertainty for oscillometric blood pressure measurements. There are three stages we consider: the first stage is pre-learning to initialize good parameters using the bagging technique. In the second stage, we fine-tune the parameters using the ensemble-based recursive methodology that is used to accurately estimate blood pressure and then measure the uncertainty for the systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure in the third stage.

result.paraphrase: Automated oscillometric blood pressure monitors are widely used to measure blood pressure in homes, offices, and medical centers, and they have received considerable recent research attention. These devices typically report a single blood pressure value and cannot show the uncertainty of the measured quantity. We introduce a new ensemble-based recursive method for quantifying uncertainty in oscillometric blood pressure measurements. The approach has three stages: first, pre-learning with bagging to initialize suitable parameters; second, parameter fine-tuning with the ensemble-based recursive methodology to estimate blood pressure accurately; and third, uncertainty measurement for systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
